newsitem.title: CANADA: New WIC director proposed by Griffiths.
newsitem.headline: New WIC director proposed by Griffiths.

text.p: WIC Western International Communications Ltd's new director was nominated by the family that controls the broadcaster, WIC's deputy chairman said Monday.
Earlier Emily Griffiths announced she was retiring as a director and that Ed Giacomelli, a managing director of Rothschild Canada Ltd, would replace her.
Griffiths is the matriarch of the Griffiths family that founded WIC and is the company's controlling shareholder by virtue of owning the majority of its voting shares.

"Mr. Giacomelli was proposed by Western Broadcasting," Klaus Priebe, WIC deputy chairman and a member of the Griffiths family, said in an interview. Western Broadcasting is the Griffiths family holding company.

Dissident shareholders have called on WIC to appoint more independent directors to its board. Oppenheimer and Co, the New York investment firm that tabled several protest motions at WIC annual meeting earlier this year, said Giacomelli's appointment did not meet its demands.
Priebe said that Giacomelli's nomination was discussed with every director on the board, his qualifications were thoroughly vetted and his election unanimously approved by the board.

Priebe disputed suggestions that Giacomelli would not act independently of the Griffiths family. "He has a duty in law to be independent....I expect him to act in the best interests of all shareholders," he said.

Giacomelli has a background in corporate finance with a specialty in the communications and broadcasting sector. Before joining Rothschild, he was managing director of investment banking services at CIBC Wood Gundy. He could not be reached for comment.
WIC chairman Edmund King was formerly chairman of CIBC Wood Gundy, a Toronto investment bank.
